common_meaning: An institution of higher education and research that grants degrees.
rrgm_bridge: A university gathers teaching and research under one structure, so that knowledge is both passed on and extended.
invariant_mi: A degree-granting institution of advanced teaching and research.

domain_entries.COG: Advanced study and the training of researchers.
domain_entries.REL: A community of scholars and students with its own governance and traditions.
domain_entries.ECO: Funded by fees, public money and research grants; costs to students vary widely by country.

count_condition: An institution recognised as granting degrees and carrying out research.
transfer_boundary: A university degree certifies completed study, not all knowledge; much learning happens outside universities. Prestige and quality are measured separately.

rrgm_bridge: Usually reports a pattern that holds most of the time, leaving room for exceptions.
invariant_mi: In the majority of cases or occasions.

domain_entries.FOR: A frequency claim: more often than not.

count_condition: A recurring situation in which one outcome happens most often.
transfer_boundary: Usually is not always; the exceptions are real.

common_meaning: The act of joining together; also an organised group of workers (a trade union); also a political union of states.
rrgm_bridge: A union joins parts so they act as one, while each part remains itself.
invariant_mi: A joining of parts into one body, or an association formed for shared interest.

domain_entries.REL: Trade unions bargain collectively for workers; marriage as a union.
domain_entries.FOR: In set theory, the union of two sets contains every element of either.

count_condition: A joining, or an association of members for a common purpose.
transfer_boundary: Joining does not erase the members; a union holds parts together, it does not merge them into sameness.
